Position Summary:
The University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) seeks a tenure-track Assistant Professor for a joint academic appointment that will strengthen interdisciplinary cardiovascular research. The position will devote 80% effort to the Sealy Department of Cardiovascular Medicine and the Sealy Heart & Vascular Institute (SHVI), with a secondary 20% appointment in the Department of Biostatistics and Data Science within the School of Public and Population Health (SPPH).
The Cardiovascular Medicine and SHVI effort will focus primarily on research and scholarly activity, with a limited component supporting quality improvement, AI-enabled clinical operations, and education. The SPPH effort will focus primarily on teaching and related academic activities that advance the educational mission of the School.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
• Develop and apply artificial intelligence approaches in cardiovascular disease and clinical operations, including opportunistic screening and large language models.
• Produce peer-reviewed publications and develop extramural grant applications that advance cardiovascular research.
• Build interdisciplinary collaborative research programs across Cardiovascular Medicine, SHVI, SPPH, and other academic partners.
• Conduct research using the Galveston Heart Study and its associated sub-studies.
• Lead and support research involving remote patient monitoring, wearable technologies, digital health, and other emerging approaches to cardiovascular care.
• Develop selected quality-improvement initiatives and implement AI-enabled tools to improve cardiovascular clinical operations, care delivery, and patient outcomes.
• Teach and participate in academic activities within the Department of Biostatistics and Data Science in support of the SPPH educational mission.
Minimum Qualifications:
• Doctoral degree in a discipline relevant to cardiovascular research, biostatistics, data science, population health, or a related field.
• Academic credentials and scholarly accomplishments appropriate for appointment as a tenure-track Assistant Professor at UTMB.
• Demonstrated ability to conduct rigorous, collaborative, data-driven research.
• Record of scientific productivity, including peer-reviewed publications.
• Strong communication, teaching, organizational, and interdisciplinary collaboration skills.
Preferred Qualifications:
• Expertise in artificial intelligence, large language models, advanced analytics, or data science applications in cardiovascular health.
• Experience with population cardiovascular health, clinical quality improvement, implementation science, or translational research.
• Experience with longitudinal cohort studies, including research comparable to the Galveston Heart Study.
• Experience with remote patient monitoring, wearable technologies, or digital health research.
• Demonstrated success in extramural grant development and interdisciplinary academic collaboration.
Academic Rank
Appointment will be at the tenure-track Assistant Professor level, consistent with the approved faculty workforce request and institutional appointment criteria.
SALARY:
Commensurate with experience.

job_1171046869dc00c4: Adjunct Instructor – Online ABSN Theory and Immersion DESCRIPTION OF JOB: Edgewood University is seeking qualified Adjunct Nursing Instructors to join our Online Accelerated Bachelor of Science in Nursing (ABSN) program. This program combines online didactic instruction with periodic in-person immersion experiences at the Edgewood University Center for Health Sciences in Madison, WI. Rooted in the Dominican tradition, Edgewood University is committed to ethical leadership, academic excellence, and inclusive, student-centered education. We are currently looking for instructors with expertise in one or more of the following areas: Medical-Surgical Nursing Maternal-Child Health Psychosocial/Behavioral Health Public Health Adult Health Perinatal & Pediatric Nursing Pharmacology Leadership & Healthcare Organizations Evidence-Based Practice Adjunct faculty in the Online Accelerated BSN program will support student learning through both virtual and in-person teaching formats. Faculty may teach online theory content, participate in immersion experiences, or both. Online theory instruction includes facilitating synchronous lectures on Tuesdays, proctoring exams on several Thursday afternoons, and holding two weekly virtual office hours. Courses run in both half-semester and full-semester formats. Online teaching experience is preferred, but training is available for the right candidate. In-person immersion faculty will teach at the Edgewood University Center for Health Sciences, located at 1255 Deming Way in Madison, WI. Faculty may lead instruction or evaluation in nursing skills, health assessment, or simulation debriefing, working with student groups of up to 8. Immersion sessions occur periodically throughout the year. First Consideration will be given to application materials received by August 25, 2025. Responsibilities: Teach and facilitate assigned nursing courses in the online and immersion formats. Provide timely, supportive, and constructive feedback. Promote a professional, inclusive, and engaging learning environment. Collaborate with course leads and full-time faculty to support consistent course delivery and academic standards. JOB QUALIFICATIONS Necessary Education or Work Experience Master of Science in Nursing (MSN), or active enrollment in an MSN program. Unencumbered Wisconsin RN license (or eligibility for licensure). Minimum of two years of full-time (or equivalent) direct patient care experience. Availability for online synchronous teaching and in-person immersion sessions in Madison. Preferred Qualifications Prior teaching experience in an academic or clinical education setting. Familiarity with online learning platforms and virtual teaching methods. Commitment to inclusive teaching practices and diverse student populations. Other Qualifications: Edgewood University, a Catholic university sponsored by the Dominican Sisters of Sinsinawa, is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to academic excellence through diversity in its faculty, staff, and students. Candidates must demonstrate multicultural competence – the awareness, knowledge, and skills needed to work with others who are culturally different from self in meaningful, relevant, and productive ways. Applicants from traditionally underrepresented populations including women and racial and ethnic minorities are especially encouraged to apply. The selected candidate must actively support the mission of the University by working with faculty, staff and students to share in our core values – truth, compassion, justice, partnership, and community. Must be authorized to work lawfully in the United States without Employer Sponsorship How to Apply Send one PDF document which includes cover letter, resume, and references with a subject line that includes the position code AIOA: Edgewood University Human Resources – AIOA 1000 Edgewood College Drive Madison, WI 53711 E-mail: humanresources@edgewood.edu Equal Opportunity Employer Return to All Job Openings

The successful candidate will have deep knowledge of and passion for the nursing profession as well as dedication to the education of future nurses. Located in historic Jacksonville, Illinois—just 30 miles from Springfield and 70 miles from St. Louis—Illinois College has been transforming lives since 1829.

job_506e535d4b377342: Postdoctoral Scholar - PIONEER Position Overview School / Campus / College: College of Arts and Sciences Organization: Physics Title: Postdoctoral Scholar - PIONEER Position Details Position Description Postdoctoral Scholar on the PIONEER Experiment The Department of Physics at the University of Washington invites applications for a post-doctoral scholar position starting in Winter 2026. This position offers a unique opportunity to contribute to forefront research at the Center for Nuclear Physics and Astrophysics (CENPA) in alignment with the NSAC 2023 Long Range Plan for Nuclear Science. The successful candidate will join a vibrant research environment on the UW Seattle campus, collaborating closely with scientists, engineers, technicians, and students at CENPA. This position is primarily associated with the PIONEER experiment, a next-generation rare pion decay spectrometer, which aims to test flavor universality up to the PeV scale. The University of Washington’s group, led by Quentin Buat, David Hertzog and Peter Kammel, is developing the active target and the calorimeter, employing cutting edge detector technologies (LGADs & LYSO) and fast electronics. Our team also carries a host of simulations to prototype the experiment and develop the event reconstruction of the experiment. The base salary range for this position will be $5705–$6500 per month, commensurate with experience and qualifications. The position is a full-time, 12-month (one-year) appointment, which may be extended (upon successful performance), subject to funding and mutual agreement. The Postdoctoral Scholar title is limited to five years, including postdoctoral experience(s) at UW and other institutions. Postdoctoral Scholars are represented by UAW 4121 and are subject to the collective bargaining agreement, unless agreed exclusion criteria apply. For more information, please visit the University of Washington Labor Relations website. About CENPA CENPA is a DOE Office of Nuclear Physics Center of Excellence, dedicated to advancing research in fundamental symmetries and neutrinos with an emphasis on discovering physics beyond the Standard Model. The Center hosts a broad program including LEGEND, He6-CRES, Project 8, Selena, PIONEER, and others. Our professional engineering and technical teams provide world-class expertise in instrumentation, prototyping, detector development, and experiment execution. For more information about CENPA and its research programs, please see the CENPA Annual Reports. Qualifications The successful applicant should have a Ph.D., or foreign equivalent, by the time they start at the University of Washington. A postdoctoral Research Associate position is available in the Environmental Nursery Production lab at the University of Florida with an emphasis on establishing fundamental research that will unlock insight into the relationship between plants, substrate and environment in outdoor nursery crop production. This position will focus on developing and publishing high-caliber research that will expand our understanding of the substrate-plant-atmosphere continuum in commercial nurseries and lead to improved production practices for ornamental horticulture. The postdoctoral associate will spend approximately 50% of their time on original, fundamental research designed collaboratively with the PI to advance our understanding of the connectivity between nursery production, the environment, and the physical world. This includes developing concepts, initiating trials, collecting, analyzing and interpreting data, with the expectation of publishing in Q1 journals. The remaining 50% of the postdoctoral associate’s time will be dedicated to advancing ornamental production practices and moving applied nursery research forward. This includes analyzing data, generating reports, and writing manuscripts for publication with the PI, mentoring junior scientists and supporting additional lab activities. These endeavors involve exploration of innovative concepts and ideas to advance production techniques, understanding of plant stress response, substrate science, irrigation technologies, and fertilizer efficiency. Thus, this position will divide their time between fundamental nursery-based agrophysics research and supporting the lab’s motto of “Applied Solutions” all with a focus on container-grown ornamental plants in open-air and protected nursery cultivation systems. Overall, this position will participate in projects focusing on plant physiology, abiotic stress, water relations, biophysics, root zone temperature management, understanding the substrate-plant-water continuum, substrate engineering, and environmental modeling. This is an in-person position in Dr. Jeb S. Fields’ lab, which focuses on developing production applications for the ornamental horticulture industry. All facilities and space necessary for success will be provided. To accentuate the postdoctoral experience, we encourage and support participation in additional collaborative research, program development, grant writing, extension, and mentoring of junior scientists. There will be opportunities to present data and build industry networks. Moreover, the postdoctoral associate will have regular dedicated collaborative mentoring time with PI for support in research and career opportunities, with the aim of securing gainful employment after the program. The postdoctoral associate position is a 12-month full-time position, and renewable annually for up to three years depending on productivity. The pay is set at $58,656 / year and comes with associated benefits. An option for 0.75 FTE is also available. Target Start Date: August 16, 2027 Application Deadline: November 30, 2026 (Applications accepted until filled or closed) Position Description The Department of Audiology at San José State University is pleased to announce a search for Department Chair beginning in August 2027. This position is a full-time tenured faculty appointment with a fractional administrative appointment as chair, responsible for the academic, administrative, and strategic direction of the program. The successful candidates will possess a substantive record of published research, teaching effectiveness, leadership experiences, and professional achievements, coupled with a demonstrated commitment to advancing health equity, interprofessional practice, and supporting diverse student populations. The Chair provides visionary academic and administrative leadership for the Department of Audiology and ensures rigorous compliance with ACAE and CAA accreditation standards while fostering a collaborative, shared governance environment with the faculty to guide curriculum, clinical training, and programmatic decisions. The Chair also serves as a mentor and advocate for the department’s faculty, actively supporting their ongoing teaching effectiveness, research productivity, and professional advancement. Established in response to the need for highly trained audiologists in California, particularly Northern California, the Department of Audiology offers a four-year, 110-unit Doctor of Audiology program with a comprehensive research and clinical training mission. Located in Silicon Valley, the program prepares students to serve the hearing and balance healthcare needs of the region’s diverse communities through comprehensive academic and clinical training. Students gain hands-on experience through the department’s on-campus audiology clinic, vestibular laboratory, clinical rotations, and externships, while also completing a multi-semester doctoral research project that integrates evidence-based practice and research with clinical education. Protein phosphorylation is an essential regulatory mechanism that controls nearly all aspects of cell division and is commonly dysregulated in human cancers.
